title: Psoriasis Treatment Classification
subtitle: By mechanism of action — topicals, phototherapy, systemic, and targeted agents

children.name: Corticosteroids
children.detail: Class I–II (clobetasol, betamethasone dipropionate) for body; mid-potency (triamcinolone) for trunk/extremities; low-potency (hydrocortisone) for face/intertriginous. Tachyphylaxis limits long-term use.

children.name: Vitamin D Analogs
children.detail: Calcipotriene (calcipotriol) and calcitriol: inhibit keratinocyte proliferation. Safer for long-term maintenance; often combined with betamethasone (Taclonex/Dovobet). Avoid on face/intertriginous (irritation).

children.name: Calcineurin Inhibitors
children.detail: Tacrolimus 0.1% and pimecrolimus 1%: off-label for inverse psoriasis, facial/genital sites. Inhibit T-cell activation without skin atrophy — ideal for sensitive areas. Avoid in infected or inflamed skin.

children.name: Coal Tar
children.detail: Antiproliferative; OTC and prescription formulations. Used for scalp disease (shampoos) and as adjunct. Less cosmetically acceptable.

children.name: Tazarotene (Retinoid)
children.detail: Topical retinoid: normalizes keratinocyte differentiation. Often combined with steroid to reduce irritation. Contraindicated in pregnancy.

children.name: Roflumilast cream 0.3% (PDE4 inhibitor)
children.detail: Topical PDE4 inhibitor approved 2022 (Zoryve): non-steroidal, suitable for intertriginous sites and long-term use. Minimal systemic absorption.

children.name: Narrowband UVB (NB-UVB)
children.detail: 311–313 nm; preferred phototherapy for plaque psoriasis. 3× weekly; response at 20–30 sessions. Safe in pregnancy. Mechanism: T-cell apoptosis, vitamin D synthesis.

children.name: PUVA (Psoralen + UVA)
children.detail: Oral methoxsalen + UVA light. Highly effective for palmoplantar and erythrodermic psoriasis; long-term risk of cutaneous SCC and melanoma. Less used now due to NB-UVB availability.

children.name: 308 nm Excimer Laser
children.detail: Targeted phototherapy for localized resistant plaques (elbows, knees, scalp). Delivers high-dose UVB directly to plaque. Fewer sessions needed than conventional NB-UVB.

children.name: Methotrexate
children.detail: 10–25 mg/week (PO or SC). First-choice traditional systemic; also treats PsA. Hepatotoxic (monitor LFTs; consider fibroscan); folate supplementation mandatory. Absolute CI: pregnancy, significant hepatic/renal disease.

children.name: Cyclosporine
children.detail: 2.5–5 mg/kg/day: rapid onset (2–4 weeks); used as bridge or for acute flares. Max 1–2 years due to nephrotoxicity, hypertension, malignancy risk. Monitor BP and creatinine.

children.name: Acitretin (Retinoid)
children.detail: 0.5–1 mg/kg/day: preferred for erythrodermic and pustular psoriasis (GPP). Teratogenic — contraception required for 3 years after stopping. Hepatotoxic; monitor LFTs and lipids.

children.name: Apremilast (PDE4 Inhibitor)
children.detail: 30 mg BID (titrated up): oral targeted small molecule. No lab monitoring required. Useful in special sites (scalp, nails, genitalia), PsA, and oral psoriasis. GI side effects; weight loss common. Not as potent as biologics.

children.name: Biologics
children.category: Moderate-severe or inadequate response to conventional

children.name: TNF-α Inhibitors
children.detail: Block tumor necrosis factor-alpha. Oldest biologic class for psoriasis. Also treat PsA, IBD (adalimumab, infliximab, certolizumab), ankylosing spondylitis. Black box: serious infections, malignancy (lymphoma), HBV reactivation. Screen for latent TB before use.

children.name: Adalimumab (Humira)
children.detail: Fully human IgG1 mAb; SC every 2 weeks. FDA-approved plaque psoriasis + PsA. PASI 75 ~60–70% at 16 wk. Reference biologic; many biosimilars available.

children.name: Etanercept (Enbrel)
children.detail: TNF receptor fusion protein; SC twice weekly or once weekly. Lower immunogenicity, milder adverse-event profile. PASI 75 ~50% at 12 wk; less potent than mAbs. Longest safety track record.

children.name: Infliximab (Remicade)
children.detail: Chimeric IgG1 mAb; IV infusion (0, 2, 6 weeks then q8w). Fastest onset. Also approved for Crohn's, UC, PsA. Highest rate of antidrug antibody formation.

children.name: Certolizumab Pegol (Cimzia)
children.detail: PEGylated Fab fragment; no Fc region → minimal placental transfer. PREFERRED biologic in pregnancy and breastfeeding. SC every 2 weeks. PsA indication also.

children.name: Golimumab (Simponi)
children.detail: Fully human IgG1 mAb; SC monthly or IV (Simponi Aria). Primarily used for PsA, AS, RA. Limited plaque psoriasis data; not FDA-approved for plaque psoriasis alone.

children.name: Ustekinumab (Stelara)
children.detail: Targets IL-12 and IL-23 shared p40 subunit. SC at 0, 4 wk then q12w (plaque) or q8w (PsA). PASI 75 ~65–70% at 12 wk. Also approved for Crohn's, UC. Favorable safety; no routine lab monitoring.

children.name: IL-17 Inhibitors
children.detail: Target the IL-17 axis (key in neutrophilic inflammation at skin). Fast onset; high PASI 90 rates. Class effect: increased mucocutaneous candidiasis; AVOID in IBD (exacerbates bowel disease).

children.name: Secukinumab (Cosentyx)
children.detail: Fully human anti-IL-17A IgG1 mAb; SC monthly (loading q2w × 4). PASI 75 ~82% at 12 wk, PASI 90 ~57%. First IL-17 inhibitor approved; also PsA, AS, nr-axSpA.

children.name: Ixekizumab (Taltz)
children.detail: Humanized anti-IL-17A IgG4 mAb; SC q2w × 12 wk then monthly. PASI 90 ~65% at 12 wk. Faster onset than secukinumab. Also PsA, AS.

children.name: Bimekizumab (Bimzelx)
children.detail: Humanized anti-IL-17A and IL-17F IgG1 mAb. SC q4w × 16 wk then q8w. PASI 90 ~85% at 16 wk — among highest clearance rates; also approved for PsA, AS. Higher candidiasis rate vs IL-17A-only.

children.name: Brodalumab (Siliq)
children.detail: Human anti-IL-17RA mAb; blocks all IL-17 isoforms (A, F, E, C). SC q2w after loading. PASI 100 rates among highest. BLACK BOX WARNING: suicidal ideation/behavior — REMS required, avoid in active suicidal ideation. Also for PsA.

children.name: IL-23 p19 Inhibitors
children.detail: Selectively block IL-23 p19 subunit → no IL-12 suppression. Q8–12 week dosing after induction; excellent long-term PASI 90/100 durability. Cleanest safety profile of any biologic class — no REMS, no BB warnings.

children.name: Guselkumab (Tremfya)
children.detail: Human anti-IL-23 p19 IgG1 mAb; SC at 0, 4 wk then q8w. PASI 90 ~73% at 16 wk; durable at 1–2 years. Also approved for PsA.

children.name: Risankizumab (Skyrizi)
children.detail: Humanized anti-IL-23 p19 IgG1 mAb; SC at 0, 4 wk then q12w. Among highest PASI 90/100 at 1 year (PASI 90 ~82–88%). Also approved for Crohn's, UC, PsA.

children.name: Tildrakizumab (Ilumya)
children.detail: Humanized anti-IL-23 p19 IgG1 mAb; SC at 0, 4 wk then q12w. PASI 75 ~64–66% at 12 wk. Smaller SC volume, well tolerated. Plaque psoriasis only.

children.name: Mirikizumab (Omvoh)
children.detail: Humanized anti-IL-23 p19 IgG4 mAb; SC q4w (induction) then q8w. Primarily approved for UC; plaque psoriasis approval pending in some regions. Strong data for IBD comorbidity.

children.name: Oral Targeted Therapies
children.category: Alternative to biologic or for mild-moderate disease

children.name: Deucravacitinib (Sotyktu) — TYK2 inhibitor
children.detail: 6 mg PO daily; selective TYK2 (tyrosine kinase 2) inhibitor; allosteric binding to regulatory domain → IL-12, IL-23, type I IFN pathway blockade. PASI 75 ~53–58% at 16 wk (superior to apremilast). No immunogenicity, no lab monitoring requirement. Not a JAK inhibitor — no black box warning. FDA approved 2022.

children.name: Apremilast (Otezla) — PDE4 inhibitor
children.detail: 30 mg BID after 5-day titration; inhibits phosphodiesterase 4 → ↑cAMP → anti-inflammatory. PASI 75 ~28–33% at 16 wk; less potent than biologics. Oral convenience; no monitoring labs. Also for PsA, oral psoriasis, Behçet's. GI side effects (N/D); weight loss; psychiatric warning (monitor mood).
